partners.mechanism_chain: CEP290 (HGNC:23992) —DISRUPTS→ Ciliogenesis (GO:0001544); KIF14 (HGNC:14067) —DISRUPTS→ Cytoskeletal Organization (GO:0007010); Ciliogenesis (GO:0001544) —LEADS_TO→ Cytoskeletal Organization (GO:0007010); Cytoskeletal Organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Meckel syndrome (MONDO:0018921); Cytoskeletal Organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Lissencephaly 4 (MONDO:0013527). Mutations in CEP290 (implicated in Meckel syndrome) and KIF14 (implicated in Lissencephaly 4) both disrupt critical cellular processes. CEP290 is essential for ciliogenesis, a process that is intrinsically linked to cytoskeletal organization. KIF14 is a kinesin motor protein that plays a crucial role in mitotic progression and cytokinesis, which also relies heavily on proper cytoskeletal organization. Therefore, disruptions in these fundamental cellular processes (ciliogenesis and cytoskeletal organization) serve as a shared mechanistic convergence point leading to the distinct yet overlapping phenotypic manifestations of Meckel syndrome and Lissencephaly 4.
